title: Document Knowledge
description: Enterprise knowledge-management platform on Azure Kubernetes Service, with document ingestion decoupled from the conversational service.
problem: Document ingestion is heavy and batch-oriented, while conversation demands low latency. Splitting them into independent services inside the cluster prevents a processing spike from degrading the chat experience.

architecture.caption: Four layers: access, container platform on AKS, AI services, and knowledge with data.

nodes.name: Public ingress
nodes.detail: TLS entry point to the cluster

nodes.name: Azure Kubernetes (AKS)
nodes.detail: Web App · Document Processor · AI Service

flow: The user comes in through the cluster ingress, which publishes the application with TLS on a custom domain.
The request reaches the Web App (React + TypeScript) deployed as a pod, alongside two internal services: Document Processor and AI Service.
The query service searches Azure AI Search, whose vectorized index powers both document search and conversation.
The AI Service orchestrates with Semantic Kernel: builds the prompt over the retrieved chunks, streams the answer and suggests follow-up questions.
At ingestion, documents enter the Storage queue; Document Intelligence applies OCR and Azure OpenAI extracts content, topics and summaries.

components.name: Azure Kubernetes Service
components.role: Cluster with three services: Web App, Document Processor and AI Service.

components.name: Managed Identity
components.role: Service access without keys in pod configuration.

components.name: Azure AI Search
components.role: Semantic index over the document repository.

insight.title: Why Kubernetes instead of App Service
insight.text: It is the only solution in the portfolio running on AKS. Isolating batch processing from the low-latency conversational service is what justifies the cluster over the App Service model used by the rest of the solutions.
